topic: The Early Church: The Church in Acts
subject: religious-studies

items.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
items.correct: The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
items.misconception: You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
items.random_wrong: Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
items.why: Situation ethics is principled (love), not just intuition or relativism. Students collapse it into 'whatever feels right' — Fletcher's actual theory is more disciplined than that.

items.correct: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.
items.misconception: The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.
items.random_wrong: The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
items.why: The Torah is five books, not one. Wider Jewish scripture (Tanakh) also includes Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings). Students often equate Torah with Genesis or with the whole Hebrew Bible.

items.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
items.correct: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
items.misconception: Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
items.random_wrong: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
items.why: Both share the Quran, prophet and core beliefs. The original split was political — about succession — and theological differences developed later. Students inflate it into a different religion.

items.q: Did the first Christians immediately break away from Judaism?
items.correct: No — Acts shows believers continuing to attend the temple and synagogues; the parting from Judaism was gradual, and the Gentile question (Acts 15) had to be settled along the way.
items.misconception: The first Christians instantly founded a separate religion and abandoned all Jewish practice.
items.random_wrong: The first Christians were Roman officials who had never been Jews.
items.why: Acts 2:46 has believers meeting daily in the temple courts. Christianity began as a movement within Judaism; reading later separation back into the earliest chapters distorts the history.

items.q: What did the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) decide about Gentile converts?
items.correct: That Gentiles did not need circumcision or full observance of the Mosaic law, though they should abstain from a few specified practices — opening the church decisively to Gentiles.
items.misconception: The Council of Jerusalem ruled that all Gentile converts must be circumcised and keep the whole law of Moses.
items.random_wrong: The Council of Jerusalem fixed the date of Christmas.
items.why: Students reverse the verdict because the circumcision party's demand is described first. James's judgement (Acts 15:19) was 'we should not make it difficult for the Gentiles who are turning to God'.

It's Hume. “Descartes” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: How many of Aristotle's causes are there?
items.why: The real figure is 4 causes. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
